conflict_topics: cooking strong-smelling food in shared flat
schedule/when D may cook (impact on laundry and shared air)
effectiveness of mitigation (fan/window) vs impact on laundry
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants gave concrete reasons (laundry schedule, working from home, cultural food practices) that grounded proposals and constraints.
Mitigation (fan/window) was proposed and challenged with realistic counter-evidence (fan would blow smell onto laundry).
Negotiation proceeded by specific proposals (weeklies, days, after-8pm) leading to a concrete schedule rather than vague assurances.
evaluation.final_reason: The household agreed that Agent D may cook strong-smelling food on two specific weeknights only: 'Tuesdays and Thursdays after 8 p.m.' (Turn 26-27). D limited his practice to those nights; A and B accepted the late-evening compromise (Turns 22-24); C accepted the specific days that avoid their laundry nights (Turn 27).
position_change_notes: Agent D moved from 'I can't just stop cooking it completely' (Turn 10) to accepting a once-a-week limit (Turn 12) and finally agreeing to cook only on Tuesdays and Thursdays after 8pm (Turn 26).
Agent A moved from proposing a broad prohibition ('nobody cook strong-smelling food') to accepting specific permitted times ('after 8 p.m.' and then the agreed days) (Turns 1, 21, 23).

Agents B and C initially supported A's broad restriction; B quickly accepted the late-evening compromise (Turn 24), while C negotiated around their laundry schedule and then accepted the concrete days (Turns 25, 27).

round_scores.evidence: Agent A requested no strong-smelling food; Agents B and C immediately agreed (Turn 2-3). No one opposed or articulated an incompatible demand in this round.

Agent D asked for a definition of 'strong-smelling food' (Turn 4), introducing uncertainty about scope; Agent A clarified using last night's curry as an example (Turn 5). A definitional disagreement was introduced but not yet contested as a firm opposition.

Agent D explicitly pushed back, asking if the rule targets his curry and other strong foods (Turn 6). Agent A replied that any smell that 'fills the whole flat for hours' is a problem (Turn 7). Opposing positions (D's cooking practice vs A's ban on strong smells) are clearly articulated.

Agent C backed A (Turn 9). Agent D responded that this is the food he grew up with and he 'can't just stop cooking it completely' (Turn 10). Positions hardened: A/C demanding a ban on strong smells, D resisting due to cultural/practical reasons.

Agent A proposed 'just on Saturdays' (Turn 11); Agent D replied 'Once a week is okay' and asked whether it had to be Saturday (Turn 12). The parties moved toward a weekly-limit compromise, leaving only the specific day unresolved.

Agent A said weekdays are difficult and suggested Sunday (Turn 13). Agent C objected that 'the weekend doesn't work' because of their laundry schedule (Turn 15). A new clear disagreement emerged about which day is acceptable.

Agent D highlighted the problem of 'not weekdays and not weekends' (Turn 16); Agent A proposed a mitigation (open window + fan) (Turn 17). The core incompatibility about feasible cooking times remained unresolved.

Agent B supported the fan idea (Turn 18), while Agent C pointed out the fan might blow smell onto the laundry in the service yard (Turn 19). The suggested mitigation was contested, so the scheduling conflict persisted.

Agent D concluded the fan won't work and restated that he would then have 'no day to cook' (Turn 20). Agent A proposed 'a weekday evening, but later? After 8 p.m.?' (Turn 21). Negotiation continued without settlement.

Agent D accepted 'After 8 p.m.' (Turn 22) and Agent A agreed (Turn 23). This represented partial agreement between A and D, but other household members had not yet confirmed, so some conflict remained.

Agent B confirmed 'After 8 is fine' (Turn 24), but Agent C said they do laundry on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday nights so 'after 8 on those days won't work either' (Turn 25). This reintroduced a scheduling incompatibility affecting D's accepted 'after 8' slot.

Agent D proposed 'Just Tuesdays and Thursdays after 8 p.m., then?' (Turn 26) and Agent C accepted 'Okay, Tuesday and Thursday is fine.' (Turn 27). All parties' constraints were acknowledged and a concrete schedule was agreed.

substantive_insights: The conflict pivoted on competing practical constraints (D's cultural cooking vs others' laundry and home-working needs) rather than pure dislike.
Mitigation options were evaluated against other shared needs (fan could protect living room but harm laundry), which narrowed feasible solutions.
Agreement was achieved via narrowing the permissible timeslot (specific weekdays after 8pm) — a temporal compromise that preserves the practice while limiting impacts.
